public_rationale: The St. Louis Fed analysis published on January 12, 2026 reports that four broad investment categories contributed 1.16 percentage points to real GDP growth in Q2 2025 [e1]. That measures a contribution to growth, not the share of GDP devoted to scaling larger language models [e1]. The analysis supplies neither an LLM-specific investment share for Q2 2025 nor recipient-level allocations showing that the investment principally financed larger-model scaling, so it does not settle either part of the claim [e1].
limitations: The broad equipment, software, R&D and data-center categories do not isolate investment in larger-language-model development.
The evidence does not establish the principal development strategies financed at investment recipients.
The contract supplies no numerical threshold for a 'very large' share.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: A very large fraction of the US economy is going into massive investments in companies that are all basically following the same strategy of scaling ever larger language models, in hopes that something magical will emerge.

statement.excerpt: Nonetheless, a very large fraction of our economy is going into the world of price wars and little moat, massive, massive investments into companies that are all basically following the same strategy of investing more and more money into one single idea, viz. scaling ever larger language models, in hopes that something magical will emerge.
statement.document_title: Could China devastate the US without firing a shot?

from_speaker: a very large fraction of our economy
all basically following the same strategy
our_interpretation: Our economy means the United States economy.
The ordinary denominator is the level of economic activity, represented by GDP, rather than the year's increase in GDP or venture funding alone.
Very large means a substantial economy-wide allocation; the speaker provides no numerical cutoff, so none is invented.
Use the second quarter of 2025, the latest GDP reporting quarter publicly available before the post.
The strategy claim concerns the principal use of investment, not simply whether recipients develop any LLMs.
The reference to something magical is rhetorical and is not treated as a claim about investors' private mental states.
criteria.support_condition: Matched investment and GDP measurements establish a clearly substantial economy-wide share, and recipient-level evidence shows that the relevant investment principally finances scaling larger language models.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Matched measurements establish only a clearly small economy-wide share, or comprehensive recipient evidence shows that the relevant investment principally finances materially different strategies.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A transparent estimate of domestic investment attributable to larger-language-model development in Q2 2025, matched to GDP for that quarter without double counting, plus recipient-level evidence of the principal strategies financed. A borderline share would also require clarification of 'very large.'
